rationale: Full English article read (774 lines). A basketball/court and season tables make the sports forecasting problem explicit. Team features feed separate core and expanded logistic regressions, merge into matchup probabilities, and sit above a chronology for season-forward validation. Initial generated gender-versus-gender output was corrected to neutral TeamLow and TeamHigh team badges, preserving the article's same-league pair orientation. No leaderboard or validation scores are depicted.
alt_en: Basketball season data becomes team features, two logistic-regression views, and blended matchup probabilities, with season-forward validation below.
alt_ko: 농구 시즌 데이터에서 팀 특성을 만들고 두 로지스틱 회귀 모델의 예측을 합쳐 대진별 승률을 구하며, 아래에는 시즌 순서를 지키는 검증을 표시한다.
prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: professional technical blog cover for a Kaggle basketball forecasting baseline; wide landscape approximately 1.9:1.
Primary request: show a clear, concrete NCAA basketball matchup probability pipeline, not an abstract illustration. A small recognizable basketball with accurate curved seam lines sits beside a simple half-court outline and a tidy season-results table on the left. The table flows by crisp arrows into a merged team-feature table in the middle, then into two compact parallel model blocks that merge into one matchup-probability output card on the right. Under this pipeline a small horizontal timeline visibly separates earlier training seasons from one subsequent validation season, communicating validation forward in time.
Concept accuracy: this article uses men and women season data, an aligned current-season cutoff, one merged team feature store, pairwise team differences, two logistic-regression feature views called core and expanded, a weighted probability blend, season-forward validation, and a checked submission. The cover should convey basketball forecasting plus auditable time-respecting data flow. Do not depict a predicted bracket as certainty or imply that the feature table alone picks a tournament winner.
Text (verbatim), only these five labels: "Season data", "Team features", "Core + Expanded", "Matchup probabilities", "Season-forward validation". Put each label beside its corresponding clear object; the last label accompanies the lower chronology strip. No other lettering or numbers, no percentages, no score, no rank, no fabricated game results.
Style/medium: polished flat technical editorial illustration, clean scientific figure craftsmanship, precise linework, simple concrete data/table/model objects, no glossy 3D. White/off-white #F7F8F7 background, slate #334A5A fine outlines, restrained teal #488A8A and muted blue #658CB2 accents. Only a very small muted basketball-colour accent if useful. No paper grain or painterly texture.
Composition/framing: one coherent left-to-right pipeline, central safe composition with generous margins, horizontal 1.9:1 cover intended for 1200-by-630 display. Large legible restrained English labels, sparing arrows, clear whitespace. A basketball/court identifies the problem immediately; simple tables and two parallel blocks identify the approach. The lower validation strip is secondary and not a chart of results.
Constraints: no long title, no logos, no brand marks, no watermark, no dense code, no tiny illegible text, no leaderboard, no trophies, no stock-photo humans, no decorative neural network, no glowing sci-fi effects, no clutter, no screenshot UI, no invented quantitative performance. Deliver one finished cover image.
revision_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit only the gender symbols in this technical basketball forecasting cover. Critical correction: NCAA men's and women's tournaments are separate datasets; the output must depict two teams within one league, never a man-versus-woman matchup.
In the rightmost "Matchup probabilities" card, replace the male and female symbols with two simple neutral team badges, each just a plain outlined shield without ornament. Place the exact labels "TeamLow" and "TeamHigh" beneath the respective badges, keeping the small "vs" between them. The two teams are basketball teams, not genders.
In the central "Team features" table, replace all male and female glyphs with identical tiny neutral circular team markers. Preserve the table's rows and colours.
Keep everything else unchanged: entire canvas aspect ratio and composition, basketball, court, season table, arrows, the two logistic-regression blocks, blend junction, lower season-forward validation timeline, all existing section labels, white background, blue/teal/slate palette, linework, and clarity. No new numbers, fabricated probabilities, performance statistics, logos, watermark, title, decoration, or extra objects. This is a narrowly targeted semantic correction.
quality_review: Generated source and final WebP inspected. Labels legible, no invented quantitative scores, no men-versus-women matchup, no logos, restrained technical palette.
